_frame_plan_note: Shot boundaries are sized from the real captured en-US-AndrewNeural narration durations (run 42315767863: 5.304/4.152/6.624/5.304/4.872/5.256s, 31.512s total), not force-fit to a fixed 30s -- the video runs as long as the real narration needs. 960 frames @30fps = 32.0s, giving each beat a small even pause (0.0813s x6) instead of being cut.

shots.visual_proof: Night road scene, two headlight-style lights near camera, painted lane stripe glowing brightly while the rest of the road stays dark
shots.narration_en: At night, these lane lines seem to glow, lit by nothing but your own headlights.

shots.visual_proof: Camera dollies toward the lane stripe, surface texture and individual glints becoming visible
shots.narration_en: Zoom in, and the paint is packed with thousands of tiny glass beads.

shots.visual_proof: Extreme close-up on glass beads embedded in the paint, an illustrative light path entering a bead, bending, and exiting back toward the camera
shots.narration_en: Light enters a bead, bends, bounces off the back, and bends again, straight back toward where it came from.

shots.visual_proof: The beaded stripe and a second, genuinely bead-free stripe side by side under the same near-camera headlight-style light: the beaded one actually retroreflects and glints back toward the lens, the plain one stays comparatively dim with no beads to bounce the light back -- a real on-screen comparison, not just two equally flat stripes under off-axis ambient light
shots.narration_en: Without those beads, the same white paint looks dull and almost disappears in the dark.

shots.visual_proof: Return to the night driving view, stripe glowing clearly ahead under headlights
shots.narration_en: That extra glow can buy a driver a crucial extra second to see the lane at night.

shots.visual_proof: Close macro beauty shot of beads glinting under the headlight-style light, no ray overlay
shots.narration_en: A tiny glass sphere, doing a precise job, on every striped road in the country.
